brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: 3 bases (piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0) are joined in a row with bolts (jointBolt x2), and all open faces have solid end caps (cap x14).
handle:0,0,0;top sits on cover:0,0,0;full;top with 3 inserts, in the middle of the caddy. The configurator checks fit only, so whether it can carry the full load hasn't been checked.
bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-div3 have 3 compartments each. Screw heaps (prop:1, prop:4) are staged in them.
The same bins give separate compartments that can hold bits. There was no bit prop, so nut and standoff heaps (prop:2, 3, 5, 6) stand in for them.

finish.summary: I built a three-cell tool caddy in a row. The middle cell has a top cover with a carry handle (fixed with 3 inserts). The cell on one side holds a full-depth 3-compartment bin, and the cell on the other side holds a half-depth 3-compartment bin, so there are six separate compartments for screws and bits. All open faces are capped with solid end caps and the joints are bolted. The finished build has 30 parts, about 1,586 g of filament, and check_build passes with no rule errors and no mesh clashes. As staging, the bins hold heaps of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs, and all of them can be seen from above. The configurator had no driver-bit prop, so nuts and standoffs stand in for bits. Standing a screwdriver or hex driver upright in the full-depth bin was refused. The configurator only checks fit, so it can't say how much weight the handle will carry when the caddy is full.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
